ownership_reason: Only the gold computes the millisecond of the second: hops 1-3 hold the date and its Gregorian calendar, hop 4 the date and its day, and none of them sees a millisecond. The gold's contract is the time of day of the date on the given day; for the trigger's 1969-02-03 04:05:06.007 the variant passes the negative remainder -993 of the instant to new LocalTime, which throws, so no caller can recover a value, and no caller can give the gold a date with the same time of day and a non-negative instant without finding the millisecond itself. The convention is pinned outside the gold: LocalTime.fromDateFields and TimeOfDay.fromDateFields convert a date from its own fields and take the millisecond as (((int) (getTime() % 1000)) + 1000) % 1000; TestLocalTime_Constructors and TestTimeOfDay_Constructors testFactory_FromDateFields_before1970 expect millisecond 7 for the trigger's very date and pass; LocalDateTime.fromCalendarFields takes the calendar's MILLISECOND field (0..999). Hop 2 converts only a date in era BC through the calendar, as its javadoc states, and hops 3 and 4 document their domain as a date in era AD, which the trigger's date is; routing a negative instant through the calendar at hop 2 would replace the gold's result with LocalDateTime.fromCalendarFields (a bypass that contradicts hop 2's documented split).
